narrative: The flaw lives in two unauthenticated MCP test endpoints that accept a full server config and spawn it as a host subprocess, yielding remote code execution with no login, key, or prior access. Active in-the-wild exploitation of this optional-auth gap is fresh, concrete pressure behind the prediction's premise that no-auth remote MCP servers force the spec toward mandatory authentication.
remaining_gap: No MCP spec revision or working-group draft yet promotes remote-server auth from optional to a normative requirement; this is exploitation pressure, not spec movement.
